key: At a family wedding in Kerala, a group of cousins
name: ch23_wedding_payasam_hint
alt: At a Kerala wedding, a smiling aunt hands payasam cups to chatty cousins in the front row and points them toward the verandah while the priest chants.
scene: A wide side view of a Kerala wedding hall during the ceremony. On the far left, a decorated mandapam with a brass lamp, banana leaves and marigold strings, where an elderly priest in a white mundu sits chanting with a small book. In the middle foreground, a front row of plastic chairs holds four young cousins in their late teens and twenties (one in a mustard kurta, one in a teal shirt, a girl in a coral half-sari, a boy in a white shirt) leaning toward each other, laughing loudly, small sound-wave squiggles above their heads. Walking in from the right is the eldest aunt, about sixty, in a cream Kerala set-saree with a gold border, grey hair in a bun, a warm smile, carrying a steel tray of small payasam cups and already handing one to the nearest cousin. A dashed arrow curves from the tray toward an open doorway on the far right that leads onto a sunny verandah with a wooden bench and a coconut palm beyond. The cousins look up grinning and a little sheepish, one with a hand over her mouth, showing they know exactly why. No one is frowning, no wagging finger. Warm golden indoor light, festive and gentle mood. Label: "GIFT, NOT GLARE" centred across the top of the image; a small word "VERANDAH" above the doorway on the right.

key: At a busy Udupi restaurant in Bengaluru
name: ch23_udupi_owner_serves
alt: In a Bengaluru Udupi restaurant, the owner leaves his cash counter to serve filter coffee to a waiting table while three chatting waiters look on, embarrassed.
scene: Interior of a busy South Indian Udupi restaurant, side view. On the far left, a raised wooden cash counter with a till and a small framed deity picture, its stool now empty. In the centre foreground, a family of three (a father in a checked shirt, a mother in a green salwar, a small boy) sits at a steel-topped table by the entrance door, a wall clock above them reading ten past eight; they look relieved and pleased. The owner, a stout man in his fifties in a white shirt and veshti with a sacred-ash line on his forehead, stands at their table setting down two steel tumblers and davaras of frothy filter coffee, a small order pad tucked under his arm. A dashed arrow traces his path from the empty cash counter to the table. On the right, near the swinging kitchen door with a serving hatch, three young waiters in maroon uniform shirts stand frozen mid-chat, one with his hand on the back of his neck, one wide-eyed, one already reaching out for the order slip the owner is holding out toward him. No one is shouting, the owner is calm and unhurried. Steam rises from the coffee. Warm evening light from tube lamps, cheerful mood. Label: "LEAD BY EXAMPLE" across the top centre of the image.

key: A school principal keeps telling teachers
name: ch23_principal_desk_corridor
alt: A school principal has moved his desk out of his inner office into the front corridor beside the clerk's window, and parents walk straight up to him.
scene: A cut-away view of the front of an Indian school office building, seen from the side like a dollhouse. On the left, an inner room with a door standing wide open and an empty space on the floor where a desk used to be, faint drag marks leading out of it toward the corridor. In the centre, the front corridor with a green-painted wall and a notice board: the principal, a man in his fifties with spectacles, a light blue shirt and a dark sweater vest, sits at his wooden desk with a nameplate, a register and a bell, now placed right in the corridor, smiling and gesturing a parent to sit. Next to him on the right is the office clerk's small window with a steel grille, where the clerk, a younger man in a striped shirt, leans out and waves a mother in a yellow saree toward the principal's desk. A father in a white shirt holding his daughter's hand (she wears a blue school uniform with two plaits) is walking in from the right side. A short dashed arrow runs from the empty inner room to the new desk spot. A small calendar on the wall reads "MON". No circular, no meeting, just the move. Bright morning light, friendly mood. Label: "OPEN DOOR" across the top centre of the image.

key: A cricket coach tells a young batter after the nets
name: ch23_coach_but_vs_and
alt: Two panels: after the coach says but, the boy walks home thinking only of poor footwork; after he says and, the boy walks home thinking of his drive and of stepping forward.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, the same pair in both halves at cricket practice nets in the evening. In each half, on the left, the coach, a fit man in his forties with a cap, track pants and a whistle on a cord, talks to a boy of about twelve in white cricket clothes holding a bat over his shoulder, pads on, helmet in hand. Netted practice lanes and a stack of red balls are in the background. LEFT panel: the coach's speech bubble shows a small bat icon with a green tick, then a large red "BUT" word in a box, then a foot icon with a red cross. The boy walks away to the right with head down and slumped shoulders, a thought bubble above him containing only the foot icon with the red cross, big and dark. RIGHT panel: the bubble shows the bat icon with green tick, a green "AND" word, then the foot icon with a forward arrow. The boy walks away upright and smiling, his thought bubble showing the bat with a tick and a footprint stepping forward toward a spinning ball. Golden evening light. Labels: "BUT" in large letters at the top of the left panel, "AND" in large letters at the top of the right panel.

key: A painting crew is redoing a flat in Pune
name: ch23_stairwell_cleanup_thanks
alt: Two panels: a flat owner bags the painters' mess in the stairwell herself one evening; next morning she thanks the mistri, and from then on the crew bags its own rubbish.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, both halves showing the same apartment stairwell landing in Pune with a flat door, a grey staircase and a window. LEFT panel, evening: paint-splashed newspapers, two empty paint tins and a roller tray litter the landing; the flat owner, a woman in her forties in a purple kurta with her hair tied back, kneels and stuffs the newspapers into a large white sack, a tin in her other hand. A neighbour's door is ajar with a frowning face peeking out. A small moon is visible through the window. RIGHT panel, next morning and after: the landing is clean. The owner stands at her door smiling, speaking to the mistri, a lean man in his forties in a paint-spotted white vest and a cap, who listens and nods proudly; her speech bubble shows a sparkling clean stairwell with a green tick and a small heart. Behind them two young painters in overalls tie up a full rubbish bag themselves next to stacked tins. A sun shines in the window. Labels: "SHE CLEANS" at the top of the left panel, "THEY CLEAN" at the top of the right panel.

key: An NCC camp in a college ground
name: ch23_ncc_shoe_polish
alt: At an NCC camp, a senior instructor polishes his own already shiny shoes and points cadets to the polish kit; next morning a row of shoes gleams.
scene: An evening and morning scene on a college ground used as an NCC camp, with olive tents and a flagpole in the background. On the left, the senior instructor, a fit man in his fifties with a neat moustache, olive uniform and beret, sits on a wooden bench polishing one black boot that is already gleaming, a tin of polish and a brush beside him, his face calm and good-humoured. Three young cadets in olive uniforms stand facing him, one with an untucked shirt and dull dusty shoes, looking down at their own feet; a small mirror-shine star sparkles on the instructor's boot. An arrow points from the instructor toward a store-room door on the right side marked with a small box icon and a polish tin. On the far right, an inset bubble shows the next morning: a neat row of five pairs of shoes gleaming with sparkles, shirts tucked, and a small green tick. No shouting, no pointing finger. Warm sunset light on the left fading to bright morning light in the inset. Label: "SET THE EXAMPLE" across the top centre of the image; the word "NEXT DAY" small above the inset bubble.

key: Your mother tastes the sambar you made
name: ch23_sambar_salt_hint
alt: At a family dinner, a mother tastes her child's too-salty sambar and kindly suggests curd rice tomorrow and a little rasam tonight; the young cook winces and notes less salt next time.
scene: A warm family dinner scene in an Indian home, viewed from the side at table height. A dining table with a steel pot of sambar, a bowl of rice, a steel tumbler of water and plates. In the centre, the mother, a woman in her fifties in a green cotton saree with a small bindi and grey streaks in her hair, holds a spoon to her lips, eyebrows slightly raised but smiling kindly. Her speech bubble shows a small bowl of white curd rice with a calendar reading "TOMORROW" and a small pot of rasam with steam, not a word about salt. On the right, her son, about twenty, in a T-shirt and kitchen apron, tastes the sambar from his own spoon and winces, eyes squeezed; a small thought bubble above him shows a salt shaker with a down arrow and the note "less salt". A salt jar sits on the table near the pot with a small exclamation badge. On the far left, the father and a younger sister keep eating calmly, unaware, showing nobody heard a criticism. Evening tube-light glow, cosy and gentle mood. Label: "GENTLE HINT" across the top centre of the image.
